Compare five-year retirement wealth under equity-funded spending and a prefunded STRIPS strategy using matched bootstrap returns.

## Scope

Results describe the supplied historical snapshot or a stated simulation. Model fit and scenario estimates are not evidence of performance on new observations. See the project README for the execution record and limitations.

```{r}
source("R/analytics_support.R")
set.seed(42)
```

```{r}
load("Data/annual_equity_returns.RData")
head(lcap_data)
```

```{r}
logret <- log(1 + lcap_data$lcap)
```

```{r}
mean(logret)
round(mean(logret), 4)
```

```{r}
sd(logret)
round(sd(logret), 4)
```

```{r}
skewness(logret)

round(skewness(logret), 4)
```

```{r}
kurtosis(logret)
round(kurtosis(logret), 4)
```

```{r}
jarque.test(as.vector(logret))
```

```{r}
n.fit <- fitdistr(logret,"normal")
mu <- n.fit$estimate[1]
sig <- n.fit$estimate[2]
n.fit$loglik
AIC.n <- 2*length(n.fit$estimate)-2*n.fit$loglik
round(AIC.n, 4)
```

```{r}
t.fit <- fitdistr(logret, "t", method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = c(-Inf, 1e-8, 1e-4))
m <- t.fit$estimate[1]
s <- t.fit$estimate[2]
tdf <- t.fit$estimate[3]
t.fit$loglik
AIC.t <- 2*length(t.fit$estimate)-2*t.fit$loglik
round(AIC.t, 4)
```

```{r}
initialwealth = 2000000
annualexpenses = 100000
```

```{r}
set.seed(437)
nsim <- 10000
nyr = 5
```

```{r}
simmat <- matrix(0, nrow = nsim, ncol = nyr)
```

```{r}
for (iyr in 1:nyr) {
  simmat[, iyr] <- sample(lcap_data$lcap, nsim, replace = TRUE)
} 
head(simmat)
```

```{r}
wmat1   <- matrix(0, nrow = nsim, ncol = nyr)
```

```{r}
initialwealth - annualexpenses
```

```{r}
wmat1[,1]   <- (initialwealth - annualexpenses) * (1 + simmat[, 1])
head(wmat1)
```

```{r}
for (iyr in 2:nyr) {
  wmat1[, iyr] <- (wmat1[, iyr - 1] - annualexpenses) * (1 + simmat[, iyr])
}
head(wmat1)
```

```{r}
wend.1 <- wmat1[, nyr]
summary(wend.1)
```

```{r}
round(median(wend.1) / 1000000, 1)
```

```{r}
lower_tail_summary(wend.1, 0.95)
```

```{r}
lower_tail_summary(wend.1, 0.95) / 1000000
```

```{r}
ci.cost = 377204
strips_payouts = 100000
```

```{r}
wmat2   <- matrix(0, nrow = nsim, ncol = nyr)
```

```{r}
initialwealth - annualexpenses - ci.cost
```

```{r}
wmat2[,1]   <- (initialwealth - annualexpenses - ci.cost) * (1 + simmat[, 1])
head(wmat2)
```

```{r}
for (iyr in 2:nyr) {
  wmat2[, iyr] <- (wmat2[, iyr - 1] + strips_payouts - annualexpenses) * (1 + simmat[, iyr])
}
head(wmat2)
```

```{r}
wend.2 <- wmat2[, nyr]
summary(wend.2)
```

```{r}
round(median(wend.2) / 1000000, 1)
```

```{r}
lower_tail_summary(wend.2, 0.95)
```

```{r}
lower_tail_summary(wend.2, 0.95) / 1000000
signif(lower_tail_summary(wend.2, 0.95)["VaR"]/1e6, 4)
```

## Interpretation limits

Independent resampling does not preserve volatility clustering. Lower-tail summaries of terminal wealth are wealth thresholds, not loss VaR. Fitted t log-return simulations can produce extreme wealth values; inspect their tails before interpretation.
